title_working: How do you pay with a coin when nobody knows what's in it?

lines.text: How do you pay with a coin when nobody knows what's in it?
lines.see: Trader's palm; pale coin lands, hand freezes

lines.text: Make it pure gold. Like this.
lines.see: Real Met stater 26.59.2 slams in full-frame

lines.text: One of the earliest known. About 8 grams, found at Sardis.
lines.see: Slow zoom on lion and bull, '8 g' tag

lines.text: Before it, a trader's coin might be half silver.
lines.see: Trader tilts a pale coin, frowning

lines.text: Weigh it? Rub it on stone? Still guessing.
lines.see: Coin streaked on black stone, streak shifting colour

lines.text: So Sardis refiners packed it in salt.
lines.see: Hands bury pale coins in salt-filled clay pot
Lidded pots glowing in small ovens
Pot cracked open, grey crust peeling away
Bright gold grain glinting in refiner's palm

lines.text: Stamp a lion and bull. Pure gold. Pure silver.
lines.see: Two die strikes: gold blank, then silver blank
Crowned king silhouette takes a bow
Gold coin drops into trader's palm (frame 1 match)

hooks: How do you pay with a coin when nobody knows what's in it?
Nobody trusted money. This is one of the earliest known coins of pure gold.
One of the earliest known coins of pure gold exists because nobody trusted money.
One of the earliest known pure-gold coins exists because the gold coins before it were a gamble.
This coin is about 1.6 centimetres long, and one of the earliest known coins of pure gold.
loop_note: Line 13 'Trust: solved. Before that...' runs into line 1 on restart: 'Before that... how do you pay with a coin when nobody knows what's in it?' Final frame (gold coin landing in the trader's palm) matches frame 1 (pale coin landing in the same palm), so the picture loops too.
changes: 0.0-5.3 (high): replaced the museum-label hook with the panel hook (question, 12 words). Line 2 'Make it pure gold. Like this.' puts 'gold' at ~4s and the real Met coin full-frame as the line starts, so the caption points at an actual object.
5.3-8.9 (high): removed 'Lydia's older coins were electrum'. No 'Lydia', no 'electrum' (named zero times); replaced with a person: 'Before it, a trader's coin might be half silver.'

8.9-10.6 (medium): cut 'But the mix varied' and its row-of-shades picture; the variation is carried by 'might be half silver' plus the shifting streak on the stone, so the mixed-colour idea appears once.
10.6-15.2 (medium): tightened to 'Weigh it? Rub it on stone? Still guessing.' (8 words); scale shot dropped, single stone-streak shot.

15.2-21.6 (medium): split the refinery run-on into four caption-sized beats (packed in salt / Baked it / The silver drew off / The gold: basically pure), each with its own picture: packing, ovens, cracked pot, gold grain.
23.3-27.2 (medium): 'Stamp a lion and bull. Pure gold. Pure silver.' as three beats with two separate die strikes; silver is set up by the refinery beat that drew the silver off.
28.9-31.7 (medium): moved 'about 8 grams, found at Sardis' to line 3, attached to the real-coin reveal and the superlative; the real photo is used once only (lines 2-3), never repeated.
Ending: new L2 'Trust: solved. Before that...' lands the payoff with light sarcasm and loops grammatically into line 1; end frame matches frame 1.
Hedges kept: 'One of the earliest known' (paired with 'pure gold' on the same coin), 'Croesus gets the credit'; no 'first ever', no claim Croesus made this coin, weight only 'about 8 grams'.
